items.text: Process tree is correct: WmiPrvSE.exe (no process-create event) → three cmd.exe (recs 9826, 9827, 9828) → whoami.exe under the third (rec 9829)
Identified remote process creation through WMI: WmiPrvSE.exe -secured -Embedding starting shells on behalf of a caller
Explained the output redirection to \\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$\__1556656369.7 (C:\Windows) as a way for a remote caller to collect output over SMB, and tied the loopback connection (recs 9830/9831) to it
Read the inbound SMB connection (rec 9825) correctly using Initiated: the remote party is 10.0.2.19, connecting to IEWIN7 on 445
Separated the tool's housekeeping (cd \, cd) from the operator's first real command (whoami /all)
Decoded 1556656369 as Unix time 2019-04-30 20:32:49 UTC and matched it to the inbound connection
Concluded from session 0, High integrity and a network logon that nobody was at the desktop and that IEUser's admin credentials are in someone else's hands
Noticed the loopback connection's timestamp is earlier than the processes it serves and didn't build the timeline on it
Tested the inventory-tool theory against what the events actually do (start shells, write to C:\Windows, whoami /all) and rejected it with reasons
Listed unknowns and recommended isolating both hosts, resetting IEUser (and shared local admin passwords), and hunting for the same pattern and source IP
